clue.text: Calendar a Latin graduate can read back to front

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: read back to front tells us to take the clue word can in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Latin scholar can read a calendar even when it runs backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read back to front' turns only the last word, 'can'; 'a' gives its own letter and 'Latin' and 'graduate' are standard abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual publication listing dates, tides and festivals is a kind of calendar.

clue.text: A day the German went to pieces?

parts.note: Sun is short for Sunday, a day of the week
der is German for the (masculine)

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a German had a breakdown one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' is only a link; the question mark warns that 'went to pieces' is not the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart into separate parts is the sense of being in pieces.

clue.text: Went one better and drew perfect circles

definitions.meaning: outdid or outperformed a rival with ease
literal reading: traced flawless round loops

explanation.surface: Someone outshone a rival by drawing flawless circles.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone easily is an idiom; read literally, it describes tracing loops.

clue.text: Average number joining the Marines

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A typical recruit is signing up with the Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual standard or typical level is the average.

clue.text: Placing female in mixed school was consistent

indicators.note: placing one thing within another signals an insertion here, completed by the following in
in says the female word goes within the word for a mixed school

parts.note: a co-ed is a co-educational school, taking boys and girls
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: Admitting a girl to a co-educational school kept the policy consistent.
explanation.definitionFit: Hung together logically, like a sound argument, is to be consistent.

clue.text: Manage to acquire a clerical cloak

definitions.meaning: to manage here is to get by, deal with difficulty
a long semicircular vestment worn by priests at services

explanation.surface: A priest manages to get hold of a ceremonial cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to acquire' simply links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting by under pressure is managing; the same word names a long ecclesiastical cape.

clue.text: Primrose has a neat petticoat

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a neat is a cow
a slip is a petticoat, an underskirt

explanation.surface: A girl named Primrose owns a tidy petticoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the old word for an ox or cow.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow spring flower is Primula veris, a member of the primrose family.

clue.text: What professional sportsmen do for recreation

definitions.meaning: professionals compete at games as their job

explanation.surface: Professional athletes are paid for what others do for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Competing at a game is a professional's work, while amusement and fun is the leisure sense.

clue.text: Male bowman in the parade

parts.note: an archer shoots with a bow

explanation.surface: A male archer takes part in a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking part in a parade walks along in step with the procession.

clue.text: Meditate away from home to find solutions

definitions.text: Meditate away from home to find solutions

parts.words: Meditate away from home to find solutions
parts.note: Meditating while out of the house is the joke; the phrase as a whole means reasoning problems through carefully to answers.

explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning a problem through carefully until reaching answers is meditating on it.

clue.text: Indisposed to find where the forecast is

definitions.meaning: a forecast is printed beneath the weather heading in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly checks the forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' links the two senses; the second is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ill is the idiom; read literally, a forecast sits beneath its weather heading.

clue.text: Blast! There's a mend in the cloth

definitions.meaning: a stitched repair of a hole in fabric

explanation.surface: Someone curses on finding a patched hole in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild expletive like 'dash it' and a woven repair to a sock share the same spelling.

clue.text: Fish makes a monk sick

parts.note: Br is short for Brother, a monk's title
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Eating fish makes a monk unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A European flatfish related to the turbot is a fish.

clue.text: Short distance from fashionable church

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A trendy church is only a short distance away.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of about two and a half centimetres is a very short length.

clue.text: Look furious in dazzling sunlight

explanation.surface: Someone scowls while squinting into bright sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Staring angrily and harsh bright light share one word.

clue.text: Arrived and left by normal desert transport

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: Someone came and went on the usual desert mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Dromedaries are the usual beasts of burden for crossing sandy wastes.

clue.text: Annoyed because officers went first

parts.note: officers hold rank, taken collectively as those of high station
led means went first, at the front

explanation.surface: People were irritated because the officers marched at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight that festers and irritates has nettled someone.

clue.text: Words added later transform religious manual

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is words added after a letter

indicators.note: transform tells us to rearrange the letters of the clue word later

explanation.surface: Revising a prayer book means adding words at a later date.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of psalms for use in worship is a devotional handbook.

clue.text: Barge encircles steamer named "The Falcon"

indicators.note: encircles means the barge word wraps round the steamer abbreviation

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge, especially on the Tyne

explanation.surface: A barge surrounds a steamship called The Falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hovering bird of prey belongs to the falcon family.

clue.text: Exercise to hang on to fellow with sex appeal

parts.note: keep means hang on to, retain
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Working out to hold on to an attractive man.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical training to stay healthy is a form of exercise.

clue.text: Yearning to put a point in the record before making gin cocktail

indicators.note: before puts the first part ahead of the next one
in places the compass point inside the record word

parts.note: a log is a record, like a ship's log
N, north, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: cocktail suggests mixing, so the letters of gin are shaken up

explanation.surface: Wanting a drink, someone notes it down before mixing a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put ... in' is the container instruction, with 'in' its signal; 'making' is just a link before the anagram signalled by 'cocktail'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong desire or craving is a yearning.

clue.text: Frenchman and I tucked into meat from Flanders

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside the word for meat

parts.note: flesh is meat
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and I eat meat in Flanders.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the Dutch-speaking region of northern Belgium describes its people and language.

clue.text: Charge to transport her gift must be negotiated

indicators.note: negotiated suggests the letters of her gift are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The fee to ship a present she gave must be agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: The fee paid for carrying cargo is a carriage charge.

clue.text: Workman induced manufacture felt

annotationWithheld.why: Workman induced manufacture felt (7) as held: HAND (workman) + LED (induced) gives the answer, defined by 'felt', but 'manufacture' has no job; likely OCR garble, and no scan or source found.

clue.text: Vestment returned by archbishop of York

indicators.note: returned means the word for vestment is read backwards

parts.note: a robe is a vestment

explanation.surface: A vestment is sent back by York's archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop of York signs with the shortened Latin name of the city, Eboracum.

clue.text: Reference some readers find extremely useful

indicators.note: some means only part of the words find extremely is used

explanation.surface: Some readers find a reference book extremely useful.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabetical list of topics at the back of a book is a reference aid.

clue.text: Opposed to displaying silver at home

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone objects to showing off silverware at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word meaning against, set in opposition to something.

clue.text: Employer turned up in a sombre suit

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read upwards, so backwards
in shows the letters lie inside the phrase sombre suit

explanation.surface: A boss appears in a dark suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The run RESU sits inside 'sombre suit'; 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who employs something puts it to use.

clue.text: It causes discomfort to current ambassador

parts.note: AC is alternating current
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Electric current is causing an ambassador discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull persistent pain is a source of discomfort.

clue.text: Leaving full-time education? Clearly not!

parts.note: Reading 'leaving education' as completing it, the joke is that this place adds a final social polish rather than ending study.

explanation.definitionFit: A private college teaching young women social graces follows ordinary education.

clue.text: Ship furnished with second rate equipment

parts.note: B is the grade for second rate, after A
rig is equipment, gear

explanation.surface: A vessel fitted out with inferior gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted square-rigged sailing vessel is a ship.

clue.text: Paid for others to be given medication

definitions.meaning: stood others a drink or meal
dosed or cared for by a doctor

explanation.surface: Others were paid for while being dosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing others a drink means paying for them; being dosed by a doctor means receiving medical care.
